transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-02
Start time (UTC): 16:00
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Marcus Li (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Sophia Ramirez (Head of Security, Veritas), Omar Khan (SRE), Elena Petrov (Identity Engineer)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Quick security review focused on SSO/SAML + SCIM provisioning and RBAC model. Customer needs BYOK/KMS info, audit log retention, and confirmation of least-privilege mappings. Agreed pilot and follow-ups.

Topics: SAML metadata exchange, SCIM attributes mapping, RBAC role slicing, audit log retention/data residency, KMS/BYOK, SOC2/ISO docs.

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Marcus Li: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um this is Marcus from Redwood Inference, i'm the AE on the account. we also have Priya from our solutions engineering team. how's everybody doing?
[00:08] Sophia Ramirez: good, thanks. thanks for making time. we uh we wanted to get into the nitty gritty today of SSO and provisioning and how you map AD groups to roles in the platform.
[00:16] Priya Nair: great, yeah i'll try to walk through our typical patterns, and we can surface any constraints you have. quick note — i'll be sharing some sample metadata and a SCIM payload near the end.
[00:25] Omar Khan: quick thing from our side, we're trying to minimize manual provisioning; want SCIM to be the source of truth. also need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, and retention is a must.
[00:33] Elena Petrov: and we have a couple identity sources: we run Okta primary, but we also have a legacy SAML idp for a few partners. so we'll need to test both.
[00:41] Marcus Li: perfect, that helps. Sophia, can you remind us of the compliance bar — SOC 2 or ISO?
[00:46] Sophia Ramirez: SOC 2 Type II is required — and we also have internal mapping to ISO controls but SOC 2 is the gating item for procurement.
[00:52] Priya Nair: ok, we're SOC 2 Type II certified — i'll attach the report. for encryption, we support customer-managed keys via KMS and HSM integrations, there's an option for BYOK with an HSM-backed workflow. a quick caveat: in some private/on-prem bundles, the key management flow differs.
[01:10] Elena Petrov: when you say KMS, do you mean GCP KMS, AWS KMS, or a generic HSM? we need to confirm we can bind to an existing HSM provider.
[01:17] Priya Nair: we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and bring-your-own-HSM in our Private deployments. hosted mode uses Redwood-managed encryption by default but can be configured for BYOK for Dedicated or Private. sometimes docs call it "Redwood Consul" in the export — sorry that's our notes quirk.
[01:32] Omar Khan: retention of logs — what's the default retention for audit logs and can we export to our SIEM (Splunk)?
[01:38] Marcus Li: default retention in hosted is 90 days, but we can extend in Dedicated/Private. export to SIEM via syslog or S3 archive is supported; Priya can show the export paths.
[01:46] Priya Nair: yes, we have a connector that pushes structured audit events to S3 and you can pick them up from Splunk. the event schema includes actor, action, resource, model_id, and request_id. some customers have asked for more, like kv-cache hits, which we can include as an optional field.
[02:00] Sophia Ramirez: and for data residency, we want the inference and logs to stay within eu-west-1 or gcp-europe-west2. is that possible?
[02:06] Marcus Li: absolutely — we have region pinning for Dedicated/Private. hosted customers can request region residency; we also have options for VPC peering and private endpoints so that traffic doesn't traverse public net.
[02:16] Elena Petrov: okay good. next on SCIM — we need to provision teams and map to least-privilege roles. how granular are roles in Redwood?
[02:24] Priya Nair: roles are tiered: admin, dev, observer, billing, and model-deployer. you can also define custom role slices. typical pattern is to SCIM provision group-to-role mapping in Okta; SCIM sends groupMembership and we map that to a role claim.
[02:36] Omar Khan: is that mapping reversible? like if someone is removed from Okta group do they lose access immediately? latency?
[02:41] Priya Nair: yes, SCIM de-provisioning removes entitlements; there's a polling cadence by default (every 5 minutes) but we can do webhook push for near-real-time in our Private deployment. hosted has a 60–300s cadence depending on load.
[02:55] Sophia Ramirez: we need assurances around orphaned sessions: if we remove a user from the role, do active tokens keep working?
[03:01] Marcus Li: tokens are short-lived (default 15m for session tokens). we also support forced session invalidation via admin action which triggers immediate revocation of K V caches. note: sometimes in the transcript exporter KV gets spelled as K V or "KV-kash" lol.
[03:13] Elena Petrov: regarding SAML metadata — what do you need from us?
[03:16] Priya Nair: we'll need the IdP metadata XML or the metadata URL, ACS URL, and the NameID format. for attribute mapping we typically use: email, given_name, family_name, groups. for role mapping we prefer a groups claim with exact group names.
[03:29] Elena Petrov: ok, i'll share the metadata and a test Okta app config.
[03:33] Marcus Li: great. Sophia, do you have any additional control requirements for RBAC auditing?
[03:37] Sophia Ramirez: yes, we need a tamper-evident audit trail, and the ability to export signed logs for compliance. also need retention SLA in contract.
[03:45] Priya Nair: we can provide signed audit bundles and time-stamped records. for higher assurance we recommend Private deployment where you control the storage and KMS. hosted can provide signed logs too but key custody differs.
[03:58] Omar Khan: what's the uplift in cost for Private vs hosted if we take BYOK and extended logging?
[04:03] Marcus Li: pricing varies — we'll send a breakdown. Dedicated with BYOK and 365-day audit retention has a premium, but most customers see predictable unit economics. i'll follow up with a pricing sheet.
[04:12] Sophia Ramirez: we also want to know about operator access and recip logging. do you allow vendor support sessions into our environment?
[04:19] Priya Nair: vendor support access is auditable and can be strictly scoped. we support time-limited ephemeral support tokens and require just-in-time access. all actions are logged, and you can require screen recording for sessions if needed.
[04:31] Elena Petrov: one technical question: when you do SCIM user create, do you create a service account in your system or do you map identities to an external principal?
[04:38] Priya Nair: we create a user record that references an external identity (idp_id). for service accounts, we provision a token that can be scoped tightly to model endpoints. service accounts can also be rotated automatically.
[04:49] Omar Khan: rotation — can we integrate that with our KMS key rotation policy? like automatic re-encryption and key roll?
[04:55] Priya Nair: yes, with BYOK we can align rotations; in Private you can push key rotations and we will rewrap data under the new key. hosted BYOK requires coordination but we do support key rotation with minimal disruption.
[05:07] Sophia Ramirez: do you have a diagram or runbook for a typical Okta-to-Redwood flow?
[05:11] Marcus Li: yes, Priya will share a runbook and sample SAML/SCIM config. we'll include a little checklist for role mappings and test cases.
[05:19] Priya Nair: i'll paste the SCIM sample in the shared drive, and include an example mapping:
- okta-group: "va-engineers" -> Redwood role: "model-deployer"
- okta-group: "va-viewers" -> Redwood role: "observer"
- okta-group: "va-admins" -> Redwood role: "admin"

[05:35] Elena Petrov: what about nested groups? Okta sometimes has nested groups under org chart.
[05:39] Priya Nair: SCIM v2 handles groups but nested groups are client-side semantics; we recommend flattening groups for mapping. we can also support custom mapping logic in Private via a transform lambda that normalizes group lists before provisioning.
[05:53] Omar Khan: for the pilot, can we run a smoke test: provision 5 users, map 2 groups, check role enforcement, and exercise revocation?
[05:59] Marcus Li: absolutely — plan the smoke test during the pilot. we'll do test cases and share expected logs.
[06:06] Sophia Ramirez: another item: do you maintain an access review cadence in the console or integrate with our governance tooling?
[06:12] Priya Nair: Redwood Console has an access review UI and can emit reports. we also support SCIM bulk-sync and we have an API to export current role membership for governance tooling.
[06:22] Elena Petrov: is there MFA required for admin roles?
[06:25] Marcus Li: yes, admin roles require MFA; we can enforce SAML assertion level or Okta policies.
[06:30] Sophia Ramirez: from procurement, we might ask for a clause on separation of duties — do you have role separation in audits?
[06:36] Priya Nair: yes, SOC 2 report outlines roles and separation. we'll flag the specific controls in the report.
[06:42] Omar Khan: small nit: how are API keys scoped to endpoints? can i create keys that only allow embeddings, and deny generation?
[06:48] Priya Nair: keys are route-scoped and model-scoped. you can create keys limited to embeddings endpoint or to a subset of models. keys can be read-only for retrieval jobs and a separate key for generation.
[06:58] Elena Petrov: any gotchas with session caching and inference privacy? like prefix caching might leak data between customers?
[07:05] Marcus Li: no cross-tenant leakage; caching is namespace-bound. we also provide per-tenant cache keys and TTLs. for extra safety we can disable shared prefix caching in Dedicated/Private.
[07:16] Sophia Ramirez: can you show an example audit event?
[07:19] Priya Nair: sure, example: { timestamp, actor_email, action: "request.infer", model: "redwood-7b", route: "/generate", request_id: "abc-123", ip: "x.x.x.x" } — the transcript might mangle the JSON braces in export.
[07:34] Omar Khan: we need the IPs to show in logs for our forensics.
[07:37] Priya Nair: included. we'll show a sample export.
[07:40] Marcus Li: ok, let's go through next steps, quick recap. Marcus: send SOC 2 and whitepaper. Priya: share SAML/SCIM runbook, sample mapping, and test payload. Elana — (Elena) share metadata and test accounts. Omar: confirm log regions and retention.
[07:56] Sophia Ramirez: timeline — procurement wants to close pilot by end of march. is that workable?
[08:01] Marcus Li: yes, pilot week of 3/8 sounds good if we get metadata and test accounts this week.
[08:06] Elena Petrov: i'll try to get the Okta metadata and a service account today.
[08:10] Omar Khan: i'll check allowed GCP regions and our SIEM ingest details.
[08:14] Priya Nair: i'll create a checklist for the pilot tests and share a calendar invite for a 60-min integration session.
[08:20] Sophia Ramirez: one last question on contract language for audit retention SLAs — who should i talk to?
[08:25] Marcus Li: i'll loop in our legal/enterprise team in the follow-up email; they'll provide proposed SLA language.
[08:30] Elena Petrov: small note — we might want RBAC to integrate with our internal ticketing system for access requests; do you have a connector?
[08:36] Priya Nair: we have webhooks and a small connector pattern for ticketing systems; we can add that to the pilot scope.
[08:43] Marcus Li: great. anything else?
[08:45] Sophia Ramirez: no, that's it. thanks.
[08:47] Marcus Li: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the items. bye.

End of call.

Notes about transcript quality: medium — some names and technical terms were auto-misrecognized (e.g., KV cache spelled as KV-kash, Redwood Console sometimes "Consul"). timestamps approximate; audio had mild crosstalk during verification steps.
